findings.title: WHO reports 33,000 acute respiratory infection cases in Gaza and year-on-year increase
findings.publisher: World Health Organization; Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
findings.affected_population_or_system: Residents experiencing acute respiratory infections in flood-affected displacement conditions; surveillance reporting period and age distribution not stated.
findings.exact_supporting_passage: There are already 33 000 cases of acute respiratory infection – higher than at this time last year.

bounded_discovery_context.discovery_method: Direct first-pass WHO Global emergency portal check and follow-through to WHO Director-General's 17 November primary statement, then checked against the immediately preceding authenticated GitHub watch heartbeat. Twelve additional targeted searches found no fresher independent confirmation.
bounded_discovery_context.duplicate_audit: The immediately previous 16:44 run recorded WFP hot-meal frequency and IOM tent clearance dimensions, not these WHO respiratory and laboratory-surveillance figures; prior Gaza incursion, medical-evacuation, detention and crossing findings were excluded.
bounded_discovery_context.material_increment: WHO quantified winter-related acute respiratory infection burden as 33,000 cases, higher than at the same point in the prior year, a previously unrecorded precise health surveillance signal.
bounded_discovery_context.caveats: WHO did not specify whether 33,000 is a weekly, seasonal or cumulative count, the reporting interval, or facility source data; no assertion of new infections occurring during the observation hour.

findings.title: WHO reports repeated refusal of laboratory supplies needed for outbreak detection in Gaza
findings.publisher: World Health Organization; Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
findings.location: Gaza Strip crossings and laboratory disease surveillance; individual sites not specified
findings.affected_population_or_system: Gaza public-health laboratory diagnostics and disease-outbreak early warning, residents relying on timely detection and response.
findings.exact_supporting_passage: We also need unhindered entry of laboratory supplies that have been denied multiple times, so that disease outbreaks can be detected and responded to early.

bounded_discovery_context.discovery_method: Direct first-pass WHO Global emergency portal check and follow-through to WHO Director-General's 17 November primary statement, then checked against the immediately preceding authenticated GitHub watch heartbeat. Twelve additional targeted searches found no fresher independent confirmation.
bounded_discovery_context.duplicate_audit: The immediately previous 16:44 run recorded WFP hot-meal frequency and IOM tent clearance dimensions, not these WHO respiratory and laboratory-surveillance figures; prior Gaza incursion, medical-evacuation, detention and crossing findings were excluded.
bounded_discovery_context.material_increment: WHO explicitly identified multiple entry denials for laboratory supplies as a hindrance to detection and early response to outbreaks, a specific health-service capacity bottleneck rather than generalized aid restrictions.
bounded_discovery_context.caveats: The WHO statement does not date the denials, identify supplies, crossings, responsible review determinations, number of consignments or quantified downstream impact. This is a reported ongoing restriction, not proof of a new denial during this hour.
